profile.name: Caspian
profile.description: I'm Caspian Reed. I grew up in Madison, studied design in Minneapolis, and spent five years in Chicago before moving to Portland. I design software for neighborhood recreation centers at Cedar Loop. Outside work I help run a repair café, play bass with friends, and take too many pictures on walks. I'm trying to keep a full life without making every evening a catch-up session.

sources.title: People in Caspian's life
sources.text:
All people, companies, conversations, schedules, quotes, and deliverables in this English sample are fictional. This is an independent American life, not a translation of another profile. No messages have been sent and no reservations or purchases have been made.

Caspian Reed — Me
American product designer at Cedar Loop in Portland. Bikes most places, plays bass on Wednesdays, and volunteers at a neighborhood repair café.
Would rather finish one useful thing than spend an evening reorganizing a to-do list.

Linda Reed — Mom
Retired public librarian in Madison, Wisconsin. Keeps a small vegetable garden and hosts family dinners.
For Tom's birthday, wants everyone at the same table instead of a surprise party with a long guest list.

Tom Reed — Dad
Retired electrician in Madison. Fixes neighbors' lamps, follows baseball, and enjoys a slow breakfast.
Turns sixty in November. Asked for a family meal and a walk by the lake, not gifts that take up space.

Emma Reed — Sister
Middle-school science teacher in Chicago. Married to Ben and usually the person who gets family dates onto a calendar.
Can leave Chicago Friday after school for Dad's birthday; needs to be home by Sunday evening.

Ben Carter — Brother-in-law
Emma's husband, a public transit planner in Chicago. Enjoys cooking and a carefully chosen board game.
Happy to drive the Chicago-to-Madison leg if someone else handles Friday dinner.

Dana Brooks — Product manager
Caspian's teammate at Cedar Loop. Talks with recreation-center staff and keeps a close eye on what a busy front desk can actually use.
The next field visit is about drop-in passes; a new dashboard can wait.

Jordan Miller — Software engineer
Builds Cedar Loop's booking tools. Lives across the river and usually bikes to the office.
Wants the staff-facing design settled before spending time on the receipt layout.

Priya Patel — User researcher
Studies how neighborhood centers welcome visitors. Shares field notes with Caspian and Dana.
Noticed staff write visitor names on scrap paper when a family arrives together.

Luis Rivera — Customer support lead
Helps Cedar Loop's center staff with day-to-day problems and knows the workarounds people actually use.
Three centers asked the same question about sibling passes; he'd like one answer he can paste into a reply.

Hannah Davis — Design manager
Caspian's manager at Cedar Loop. Protects time for visits to actual customer sites.
Asked Caspian to show two concrete examples at the next design review, with the tradeoff beside each.

Marcus Brown — Marketing teammate
Writes Cedar Loop's customer newsletter and works closely with support.
Won't announce a feature until the people answering customer questions have seen the note.

Emily Carter — Accessibility consultant
Independent designer who joins Cedar Loop's reviews. Focuses on readable instructions, keyboard access, and ordinary language.
Suggested keeping the visitor's name visible while staff switch between family members.

Maya Thompson — Close friend
Portland ceramic artist and Caspian's friend since a neighborhood potluck. Runs weekend classes in a shared studio.
Likes plans with one clear meeting place and enough room to change their minds.

Alex Kim — Climbing friend
Mechanical engineer and regular at Caspian's climbing gym. Also enjoys an unhurried breakfast after a ride.
Usually free Sunday mornings; prefers checking in before adding another person to a plan.

Sarah Johnson — Neighbor
Lives downstairs and helps organize the building's little courtyard garden.
Works early shifts. Asked for noisy shelf assembly before 8 p.m., especially on Sundays.

Chris Martinez — Repair café volunteer
Bike mechanic who volunteers at the neighborhood repair café. Brings hand tools and an impressively organized patch kit.
Can run the bike table for two hours in October, but needs one other volunteer for intake.

Olivia Parker — Community center coordinator
Coordinates events at the fictional Maple Street Community Center in Portland.
The repair café can use the back room on October 17 from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m.; teardown must finish by 1:30.

Noah Wilson — College friend
Graphic designer in Chicago. Shared a studio with Caspian in college and still sends him questionable album covers.
Would like to meet for dinner when Caspian passes through Chicago in November, without turning it into another big event.

Rachel Adams — Book-club friend
Bookseller in Portland. Hosts a six-person book group at a neighborhood café.
Likes everyone to suggest one question rather than arrive with a polished interpretation.

Sam Taylor — Bandmate
Drummer in Caspian's casual three-piece band. Rehearses in a rented room on Wednesday evenings.
Wants to record one clean take of their new song before worrying about a gig.

Grace Lee — College friend and photographer
Seattle-based photographer who studied with Caspian in Minneapolis. They swap small photo projects by mail.
Encouraged Caspian to finish a twelve-photo neighborhood zine before buying another camera.

Matt Evans — Landlord
Owns the duplex where Caspian rents an upstairs apartment. Handles building repairs himself when he can.
Freestanding shelves are fine; wall anchors need a plan first because there are old pipes in one wall.

sources.title: A few things about me
sources.text:
I'm American and grew up in Madison. My parents still live in the house near the library. I studied design in Minneapolis from 2013 to 2017, then moved to Chicago for a job at a small design studio. I liked the people more than the late nights. In 2022 I moved to Portland and joined Cedar Loop, which makes booking software for neighborhood recreation centers.

I don't own a car. My bike is my usual way around Portland, with the bus as a backup when the weather or the load calls for it. Wednesday nights are band rehearsal, 6:30 to 8:30. I try to keep work from spilling over that slot. I volunteer at the repair café once a month; I help with intake and keeping people from waiting in the wrong line.

The thing I'm trying to get better at is saying what I can actually finish this week. I like short notes that start with the decision. Give me a couple of good choices, not twelve. If something needs to be sent, booked, or bought, let me see the actual details first.

sources.title: Talking with Mom about Dad’s birthday
sources.text:
Linda Reed: Do you know yet if you can come for your dad's birthday? No pressure to fly in for one dinner.
Caspian Reed: I want to. I'm looking at the weekend of the 14th. Could stay with you if the spare room isn't full of tomato boxes.
Linda Reed: Only one tomato box. I'll move it.
Caspian Reed: Can we keep Saturday pretty quiet? Dinner at home and maybe the lake if it's nice.
Linda Reed: That is exactly what he wants. Emma said Friday after school is the earliest she can leave.
Caspian Reed: Okay. I'll work around that and send actual times once I've picked a flight.
Linda Reed: Good. And tell me one thing you want to eat besides breakfast potatoes.

sources.title: Asking Dad what he’d like for his birthday
sources.text:
Caspian Reed: Mom says you're vetoing presents.
Tom Reed: I'm not vetoing pie.
Caspian Reed: Very specific loophole. Apple?
Tom Reed: Apple is good. Mostly I'd like to have everybody here for a meal.
Caspian Reed: Then no surprise restaurant reservation. We can cook and walk by the lake Saturday.
Tom Reed: Perfect. There's a lamp in the garage we can take a look at if you get bored.
Caspian Reed: You really know how to sell a vacation.

sources.title: Comparing travel plans with Emma
sources.text:
Emma Reed: I can get out of school around 4 on Friday. Ben can drive us up after that.
Caspian Reed: Would picking me up in Chicago make the drive annoying?
Emma Reed: Depends where and when. Please don't book something that lands at 5:15 and assume we can be in Madison for dinner at 7.
Caspian Reed: Fair. I'll compare a Thursday arrival with flying straight to Madison. Budget is about $600 for travel.
Emma Reed: Thursday would give you time to see Noah too. We need to be home Sunday by 7.
Caspian Reed: I'll leave Sunday lunch optional and build in the drive back. No packed itinerary.

sources.title: Planning Friday dinner with Ben
sources.text:
Ben Carter: For your dad's weekend: I can drive Friday and Sunday. Can you handle something easy for Friday dinner?
Caspian Reed: Yeah. Something Mom doesn't have to babysit while people arrive.
Ben Carter: Chili? I can bring cornbread. Emma doesn't get an actual lunch break some Fridays, so let's not wait until nine.
Caspian Reed: Chili it is. I'll make it when I get to Madison, if Thursday works. Otherwise we can prep ahead.
Ben Carter: Send me the grocery list when you've got one. No giant spreadsheet required.
Caspian Reed: You'll get a small list. I make no promises about whether it has headings.

sources.title: Planning the family check-in review with Dana
sources.text:
Dana Brooks: Can we use tomorrow's review for drop-in passes? Lakeside's front desk is still writing sibling names on paper.
Caspian Reed: Yes. Priya saw the same thing Tuesday. Staff lose track of which child they're adding when they switch screens.
Dana Brooks: I don't think we need a family dashboard to solve that.
Caspian Reed: Agreed. I'll bring one option with a persistent family list and one with an add-another flow. Same scenario in both.
Dana Brooks: Good. We have thirty minutes, and Jordan needs a decision before Monday.
Caspian Reed: I'll lead with the choice and the reason. Screens after that.

sources.title: Working through the back button with Jordan
sources.text:
Jordan Miller: The family list is straightforward. Letting people edit names inside the receipt is a different rabbit hole.
Caspian Reed: Let's keep editing in the form. Receipt can stay read-only.
Jordan Miller: Works for me. What happens if a parent adds three kids and backs up?
Caspian Reed: Keep all three names. Back should mean go back, not start over. I'll draw that state explicitly.
Jordan Miller: Thank you. That's the part I'd otherwise guess.
Caspian Reed: I'll post the two states before lunch. Feel free to call me if one doesn't make sense.

sources.title: Reading Priya’s notes from Lakeside
sources.text:
Priya Patel: Pulled the notes from Lakeside. We watched seven family check-ins. In four, the receptionist wrote names on paper first.
Caspian Reed: Was that because of the screen or because the line was long?
Priya Patel: Both. The screen only shows one child at a time, and they didn't want to ask the parent to repeat names.
Caspian Reed: Useful distinction. I'm going to keep the family names visible, but I won't claim it fixes the whole queue.
Priya Patel: Exactly. Also, Kim at the desk asked us to stop calling it a household object.
Caspian Reed: Fair request. 'Family' on the screen, boring database names kept out of it.

sources.title: Drafting an explanation of the pass change
sources.text:
Luis Rivera: Could you send me the plain-English version of the pass change? Three centers have asked.
Caspian Reed: It'll keep the family list on screen while staff add passes. Same payment step as now.
Luis Rivera: Does it save a family for next time? That's what the last caller thought.
Caspian Reed: No, just this visit. We should say that clearly in the note.
Luis Rivera: Please do. And give me one example I can use without opening Figma.
Caspian Reed: I'll write it around a parent bringing two kids, and send you the draft before Marcus uses it.

sources.title: Discussing the design review with Hannah
sources.text:
Hannah Davis: How was the center visit?
Caspian Reed: Helpful. Less elegant than our diagram, in a good way. One receptionist can talk to three people while finding a pen.
Hannah Davis: That's the job we're designing for. Show that messiness on Friday, not just the happy path.
Caspian Reed: Two options, same family checking in, and what happens when they back up.
Hannah Davis: Perfect. Don't spend Thursday night polishing the slide transitions.
Caspian Reed: I wasn't going to, but now you have successfully removed the temptation.

sources.title: Checking the newsletter wording with Marcus
sources.text:
Marcus Brown: Is 'faster family check-in' okay for the newsletter heading?
Caspian Reed: Maybe, but we haven't timed it. 'Keep a family's passes together' is something we can actually show.
Marcus Brown: Less punchy. More true. I can work with that.
Caspian Reed: Luis should read the draft first. People may think it saves the family for a future visit.
Marcus Brown: I'll put 'for this visit' in the first paragraph. Send me the final screen when Jordan has it.
Caspian Reed: Will do. We're aiming for next week's field check, not announcing a date yet.

sources.title: Reviewing names and error messages with Emily
sources.text:
Emily Carter: I can follow the keyboard order now. One thing: the selected child's name disappears when the payment panel opens.
Caspian Reed: I'll keep the name above the total. Does the error need to repeat it too?
Emily Carter: Yes. 'Choose a pass for Jamie' tells staff what to fix. 'Missing selection' doesn't.
Caspian Reed: That's a better sentence. I'll change the other two errors while I'm here.
Emily Carter: Great. Send the clickable version afterward; screenshots won't tell me where focus lands.
Caspian Reed: Tomorrow morning. I'm logging off for rehearsal soon.

sources.title: Meeting Maya for coffee and photo editing
sources.text:
Maya Thompson: Want to get coffee Sunday? I have a class at noon but my morning is free.
Caspian Reed: Yes. Eastside at 9:30? I can bring the little photo prints.
Maya Thompson: The ones you've been 'almost done' with since August?
Caspian Reed: Those exact prints. I need someone to remove six from the pile.
Maya Thompson: Happy to be ruthless. No laptop though.
Caspian Reed: Deal. Paper photos and coffee. Very advanced workflow.

sources.title: Arranging a Sunday climb with Alex
sources.text:
Alex Kim: Gym Sunday morning? I'm thinking 10, nothing heroic.
Caspian Reed: Coffee with Maya first. Could do 10:30 if you don't mind me arriving fully caffeinated.
Alex Kim: 10:30 works. My friend Erin might come. Okay if I invite her?
Caspian Reed: Of course. Just tell her I am firmly in the climb-three-routes-and-chat camp.
Alex Kim: That is also her camp.
Caspian Reed: Excellent. We have built a very achievable team.

sources.title: Checking a shelf-assembly time with Sarah
sources.text:
Caspian Reed: I might put a shelf together this weekend. What time is least annoying downstairs?
Sarah Johnson: Saturday afternoon is fine. Sunday I'm on an early shift, so quieter after eight would be lovely.
Caspian Reed: Saturday 2 to 4, then. It's freestanding, mostly the tiny wrench situation.
Sarah Johnson: The tiny wrench is somehow the loudest tool.
Caspian Reed: I'll put a blanket under it. Also happy to move the courtyard planters first.
Sarah Johnson: That would be great. They're heavy after the rain.

sources.title: Planning the bike table with Chris
sources.text:
Chris Martinez: I'm in for October 17. Can do the bike table 10 to noon.
Caspian Reed: Amazing. Olivia has the back room until one. What do you need from us?
Chris Martinez: Two tables, a floor pump, and someone doing intake so I don't stop every five minutes.
Caspian Reed: I can handle intake for the first hour. Need to find someone for eleven.
Chris Martinez: Cap it at six bikes to start. Better to finish six than have twelve people annoyed.
Caspian Reed: Six slots. Walk-ins can still ask questions, but we won't promise a repair.

sources.title: Confirming the repair café room and budget
sources.text:
Olivia Parker: Back room is yours October 17, 10 to 1. A kids' class needs it at two, so please be packed by 1:30.
Caspian Reed: Thanks. We'll stop taking new items at noon and use the last half hour for cleanup.
Olivia Parker: Good. No extension cords across the main doorway this time.
Caspian Reed: We'll keep the electrical table along the back wall. I'll put it on the room sketch.
Olivia Parker: The center can cover $150. Anything beyond that needs to come from your group's budget.
Caspian Reed: Our total cap is $320. I'll send a simple supply list with who brings what.

sources.title: Tentatively arranging dinner with Noah
sources.text:
Caspian Reed: Possibly in Chicago November 12, on the way to Dad's birthday. Dinner?
Noah Wilson: Yes, if by dinner you mean noodles and complaining about typography.
Caspian Reed: I was hoping we'd matured, but apparently not.
Noah Wilson: I can do Thursday after seven. Friday I'm helping my sister move.
Caspian Reed: Thursday sounds good. Don't block the whole night until I've actually booked.
Noah Wilson: Text me when it's real. I'll pick somewhere near the train so you don't spend the evening in a rideshare.

sources.title: Getting ready for Thursday’s book group
sources.text:
Rachel Adams: Book group next Thursday, 7 at the café. Bring one question, not a report.
Caspian Reed: You're taking away my ability to overprepare.
Rachel Adams: Yes. Last time you brought page flags in three colors.
Caspian Reed: This time my question is why nobody in this book ever just goes home.
Rachel Adams: Honestly, good question.
Caspian Reed: I'll finish the last forty pages on the bus. See you Thursday.

sources.title: Planning Wednesday’s rehearsal with Sam
sources.text:
Sam Taylor: Wednesday: can we just work on the new song instead of playing the whole set?
Caspian Reed: Please. I still lose the count after the second chorus.
Sam Taylor: Let's loop that bit, then record one take. Room is booked 6:30 to 8:30.
Caspian Reed: I'll be there by 6:20. No work call this week.
Sam Taylor: Nice. I'll bring the little recorder.
Caspian Reed: And I'll bring the cable I forgot last time. Putting it in the bag now.

sources.title: Talking through the photo zine with Grace
sources.text:
Grace Lee: How many photos are in your twelve-photo zine now?
Caspian Reed: Twenty-six. In my defense, twelve is a difficult number.
Grace Lee: It's actually one of the more straightforward numbers.
Caspian Reed: Maya helped me cut six. I think the bus-window shots belong together.
Grace Lee: Then start there. Make a cheap print before you touch the color again.
Caspian Reed: Okay. Twelve images, folded paper, no new equipment. Hold me to it.
Grace Lee: Happily. Mail me one when it's done.

sources.title: Asking Matt about the shelf and window latch
sources.text:
Caspian Reed: Would a freestanding bookcase by the north wall be okay? About 5 feet tall, no drilling planned.
Matt Evans: Yes. If the instructions call for anchors, send me a picture of the spot first. Old pipes are in part of that wall.
Caspian Reed: Got it. I'll choose something low enough to use safely without guessing about the wall.
Matt Evans: Thanks. Also, I can look at the sticky window latch Friday around four.
Caspian Reed: I'll be home. It's still usable, just takes two hands.
Matt Evans: I'll text before I come by.

sources.title: Checking the family’s birthday-weekend plans
sources.text:
Emma Reed: Birthday weekend check: November 13 to 15. Ben and I drive up Friday after school.
Tom Reed: The birthday person requests pie and no singing in a restaurant.
Linda Reed: We can manage that.
Caspian Reed: I'm comparing flights. Saturday at home and a lake walk if the weather cooperates?
Ben Carter: I'll bring a board game with rules shorter than the meal.
Emma Reed: Sunday we'll need to leave by about 2 to be home in time.
Caspian Reed: Then lunch is optional, no cross-town detour. I'll put the actual arrival times in here once booked.
Tom Reed: Sounds good. Really looking forward to it.

sources.title: Dividing up repair café shifts
sources.text:
Caspian Reed: We have the back room October 17, 10 to 1. Chris can do six bike slots, with intake help.
Chris Martinez: I bring tools and a pump. Please don't put 'all repairs welcome' on the flyer.
Sarah Johnson: I can do intake 11 to noon. Can we have a spot for people who just want advice?
Olivia Parker: Yes, small table by the windows. Main doorway has to stay clear.
Caspian Reed: Great. I'll do 10 to 11, Sarah does 11 to noon. New items stop at noon; cleanup starts at 12:30.
Chris Martinez: That's doable. I'd rather send someone home with an honest answer than rush a job.
Sarah Johnson: Can the flyer say to bring the item, not just a photo of it? Last time was confusing.
Caspian Reed: Adding that, plus a line that a repair isn't guaranteed.

sources.title: Agreeing on the family check-in changes
sources.text:
Caspian Reed: Review decision: keep the family list on screen; add one child at a time; payment stays as it is.
Dana Brooks: What are we deliberately leaving out?
Caspian Reed: Saved families for a later visit, receipt editing, and a new dashboard. This only helps today's check-in.
Jordan Miller: I can build that for the field check next Thursday if copy is final Monday.
Priya Patel: I'll ask Lakeside for a quiet hour. We should test a family adding a child after backing up.
Luis Rivera: I'll read the staff note before it goes out. Please put 'for this visit' near the top.
Caspian Reed: Done. I'll send the note as a draft, not an announcement.
Dana Brooks: Good. I'll confirm the field visit with the center.

sources.title: Making a Sunday coffee and walk plan
sources.text:
Maya Thompson: Weather looks decent Sunday morning. Coffee, then a short walk?
Alex Kim: I'm up for it after ten. I can skip the gym one week.
Caspian Reed: Meet outside the café at 10:15? I need to be back by one to call my parents.
Maya Thompson: That gives us plenty of time. No destination?
Caspian Reed: Just along the river and back. I am resisting the urge to make a route.
Alex Kim: Proud of you.
Maya Thompson: Bring the prints anyway. A bench can be a gallery.

sources.title: Offering to move the courtyard planters
sources.text:
Sarah Johnson: Could either of you help move the big planters Saturday before it gets colder?
Caspian Reed: I can do 1:30, before the shelf project.
Matt Evans: I'll bring a hand truck. Please don't try carrying the tall one down the steps.
Sarah Johnson: Thank you. Also have spare rosemary if anyone wants some.
Caspian Reed: Yes please. My current plant collection is mostly empty pots.
Matt Evans: Rosemary will improve the average.

sources.title: Planning the ending of the new song
sources.text:
Sam Taylor: Same room tomorrow, 6:30. I uploaded the rough recording.
Alex Kim: The chorus is good. The ending sounds like three different exits.
Caspian Reed: Accurate. Can we try stopping together after the last four bars?
Sam Taylor: Yes. No dramatic fade-out, we are not that band.
Alex Kim: I'll bring the guitar stand this time.
Caspian Reed: Bass cable is already packed. A historic first.

sources.title: Choosing the photo order before printing
sources.text:
Caspian Reed: Here are the twelve. Bus window opens, empty basketball court closes.
Grace Lee: That order makes sense. I'd swap the two middle street corners; the light moves more naturally.
Maya Thompson: Keep the blurry bakery window. It's the only one that feels warm.
Caspian Reed: I nearly cut that one. Okay, it stays.
Grace Lee: Now print a rough copy. Screen decisions are done.
Caspian Reed: Friday lunch break. Ten cheap copies, then I can stop calling this a work in progress.

sources.title: Comparing the return flights for November
sources.text:
Caspian Reed: Thursday in Chicago seems best. Noah, dinner after seven still possible?
Noah Wilson: Yes. Pick a flight first and I'll keep dinner near wherever you're staying.
Emma Reed: You can use our couch Thursday. Ben and I leave for Madison around 4:30 Friday.
Caspian Reed: That saves a hotel. I'll work from your kitchen Friday morning if that's okay.
Emma Reed: Fine. The good chair is mine when I get home, though.
Caspian Reed: Understood. Still choosing between two return flights; one is cheaper but leaves too little time after the drive.

sources.title: Reviewing the staff note with Luis and Marcus
sources.text:
Caspian Reed: Draft is in the project. One correction: 'family list' isn't a saved profile. It clears after payment.
Luis Rivera: I added a sentence saying staff can check the names before charging. That's usually the question.
Marcus Brown: Can I use the two-kid example in the newsletter later?
Caspian Reed: Yes, after the field check. Please don't use the date in this draft as a launch date.
Marcus Brown: Noted. Draft stays a draft.
Luis Rivera: This version I can explain over the phone. Much better.

sources.title: A few dates from my life
sources.text:
1995 — Growing up in Madison
I grew up near the public library in Madison with Mom, Dad, and my younger sister Emma.

2013-09 to 2017-05 — Studying design in Minneapolis
I moved from Wisconsin to Minneapolis to study design at the University of Minnesota. Noah and Grace were in the shared studio, and we became friends there.

2017-07 to 2022-04 — My first design job in Chicago
I joined a small design studio in Chicago and learned to explain my choices to clients. I liked the team, but the late nights were one reason I eventually moved on.

2022-05 — Moving to Portland
I moved to Portland for a product design job at Cedar Loop and rented the upstairs apartment in Matt’s duplex.

2022-06 — Starting at Cedar Loop
I started working with Dana, Jordan, and Priya on booking software for neighborhood recreation centers.

2023-04 — Starting at the repair café
I began volunteering at the repair café and met Chris and Olivia. I helped with intake, signs, and queues so people could find the right volunteer.

2024-02 — Starting Wednesday band rehearsals
Sam, Alex, and I started rehearsing on Wednesday nights. I’ve tried to keep that evening free even during busy weeks at work.

2024-08 — Switching to a bike and public transit
I stopped keeping a car and began using a bike and public transit for everyday trips. Visiting family now takes more planning around flights and shared rides.

2026-08 — Starting a neighborhood photo zine
I started putting together photos from walks and bus rides. Grace and Maya encouraged me to choose 12 and make a rough print.

2026-09-24 — Visiting Lakeside’s front desk
I watched a busy family check-in at Lakeside. After the visit, I focused on keeping family names visible during the current visit instead of adding a dashboard.

Six bike appointments run from 10 to noon. Advice table stays open until noon. Cleanup begins at 12:30; room handed back by 1:30.

sources.title: Two rough November travel options
sources.text: All times and prices in this note are fictional planning examples, not live availability. Option A: Thursday evening arrival in Chicago; $385 round-trip flight estimate, $32 airport transit, $60 contribution to shared gas, $55 food allowance, $60 buffer. Stay on Emma and Ben’s couch Thursday. Leave Chicago Friday around 4:30 p.m. for Madison; depart Madison Sunday around 2 p.m. Option B: fly directly to Madison; $510 flight estimate, $40 ground transport, $55 food allowance, $60 buffer. A late Sunday return is preferable; the cheaper early return conflicts with the drive from Madison. Nothing has been booked.

sources.title: Work-corner measurements and limits
sources.text: The north-wall space measures 58 inches wide. Keep the window and radiator clear. Current desk is 42 inches wide. Budget cap is $180. A freestanding low shelf is preferred; no wall anchors without Matt’s approval. Fictional shopping estimates: a used 30-inch-wide low shelf $65, task lamp $35, cable clips $12, delivery or transport reserve $25. Caspian does not own a car. Sarah is fine with assembly Saturday 2–4 p.m.; avoid noise after 8 p.m. Sunday. Check shelf depth and manufacturer installation instructions before choosing it.

events.title: Talking with Mom about Dad’s birthday
events.description: Mom and I talked about visiting for Dad’s birthday on the weekend of November 14. We’d like to have dinner at home and walk by the lake if the weather is good. I’m still comparing flights and will send arrival times once I choose one.

events.title: Asking Dad what he’d like for his birthday
events.description: Dad would like an apple pie and a meal with everyone at home. We talked about cooking and taking a walk by the lake on Saturday. There’s no restaurant reservation to make.

events.title: Comparing travel plans with Emma
events.description: Emma and Ben can leave Chicago after school on Friday and need to be home by 7 p.m. Sunday. I’m comparing arriving in Chicago on Thursday with flying directly to Madison, with about $600 for travel. Sunday lunch can stay optional.

events.title: Planning Friday dinner with Ben
events.description: Ben offered to drive between Chicago and Madison on Friday and Sunday. I’ll handle chili for Friday dinner, and he’ll bring cornbread. If I arrive Thursday, I can cook in Madison; otherwise we’ll prepare ahead. I still need to send the grocery list.

events.title: Planning the family check-in review with Dana
events.description: Dana wants the next review to focus on drop-in passes. Staff at Lakeside lose track of children’s names when switching screens. I’ll compare a list that stays visible with an add-another flow, using the same family in both. We have 30 minutes, and Jordan needs a decision before Monday.

events.title: Working through the back button with Jordan
events.description: Jordan and I agreed that name edits should stay in the form and the receipt should remain read-only. Going back after adding three children should keep all three names. I’ll send the two screen states before lunch so he doesn’t have to guess.

events.title: Reading Priya’s notes from Lakeside
events.description: Priya observed 7 family check-ins. In 4 of them, staff wrote names on paper before entering them. The screen shows only one child at a time, and the queue also adds pressure. I’ll keep the family names visible and use “Family” in the interface, without claiming that this solves the whole queue.

events.title: Drafting an explanation of the pass change
events.description: Luis has had the same question from 3 centers. I’ll write an example with a parent and two children: the family list stays visible while adding passes, payment works as before, and the list is only for this visit. Luis will see the draft before Marcus uses it.

events.title: Discussing the design review with Hannah
events.description: Hannah asked me to show what happens at a busy front desk, including what happens when staff go back. I’ll use the same family to compare two options. She also reminded me that I don’t need to spend the evening polishing slide transitions.

events.title: Checking the newsletter wording with Marcus
events.description: Marcus suggested “faster family check-in,” but we haven’t measured the time. We agreed to describe keeping a family’s passes together instead. Luis should review the draft, and it needs to say “for this visit.” We’re preparing for a field check, not announcing a launch date.

events.title: Reviewing names and error messages with Emily
events.description: Emily can follow the keyboard order now, but the selected child’s name disappears when the payment panel opens. I’ll keep it above the total and use the name in the error message. She asked for the clickable version tomorrow morning so she can check where focus goes.

events.title: Meeting Maya for coffee and photo editing
events.description: Maya and I agreed to meet at Eastside on Sunday at 9:30 a.m., before her noon class. I’ll bring the photo prints so she can help me cut six from the selection. We’re leaving the laptop at home.

events.title: Arranging a Sunday climb with Alex
events.description: Alex and I settled on 10:30 a.m. at the climbing gym after my coffee with Maya. His friend Erin may join us. I’m planning a few routes and some time to chat, rather than a long session.

events.title: Checking a shelf-assembly time with Sarah
events.description: Sarah is fine with me putting the shelf together on Saturday from 2 to 4 p.m. She has an early shift on Sunday and asked for quiet after 8 p.m. I offered to help move the courtyard planters first and put a blanket under the shelf while assembling it.

events.title: Planning the bike table with Chris
events.description: Chris can help at the repair café on October 17 from 10 a.m. to noon. He needs two tables, a floor pump, and someone on intake. We’re starting with 6 bike appointments. I can cover intake for the first hour; the second hour still needs someone.

events.title: Confirming the repair café room and budget
events.description: Olivia confirmed the back room for October 17, 10 a.m. to 1 p.m., with everything packed by 1:30. We’ll stop taking new items at noon and keep the doorway clear. The center can contribute $150 toward our $320 budget; I’ll send a supply list showing who brings each item.

events.title: Tentatively arranging dinner with Noah
events.description: I may pass through Chicago on November 12. Noah is free for dinner after 7 p.m. that Thursday and can choose somewhere near the train. I haven’t booked a flight, so we’re keeping the plan tentative.

events.title: Getting ready for Thursday’s book group
events.description: Rachel confirmed the book group for next Thursday at 7 p.m. at the café. Everyone should bring one question. I still have 40 pages to read and plan to finish them on the bus.

events.title: Planning Wednesday’s rehearsal with Sam
events.description: Sam and I want to work on the new song, especially the section after the second chorus, then record a take. The room is booked from 6:30 to 8:30 p.m. I’ll arrive by 6:20, and I’ve packed the bass cable I forgot last time.

events.title: Talking through the photo zine with Grace
events.description: I still have 26 photos for a zine meant to contain 12. Grace suggested starting with the bus-window pictures and making a cheap print before more color editing. I agreed to use folded paper and the equipment I already have, then mail her a copy when it’s done.

events.title: Asking Matt about the shelf and window latch
events.description: Matt is fine with a freestanding shelf by the north wall. If it needs anchors, he wants a photo of the spot first because of the old pipes. He can also check the sticky window latch around 4 p.m. Friday and will text before coming over.

events.title: Checking the family’s birthday-weekend plans
events.description: We confirmed November 13–15 for Dad’s birthday weekend. Emma and Ben will drive up after school on Friday. Saturday is for a meal at home and a possible lake walk; they need to leave around 2 p.m. Sunday. I’m still comparing flights.

events.title: Dividing up repair café shifts
events.description: We have the back room on October 17 from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. I’ll cover intake from 10 to 11, then Sarah from 11 to noon. Chris can take 6 bike appointments. New items stop at noon and cleanup starts at 12:30. The flyer will ask people to bring the item and explain that a repair isn’t guaranteed.

events.title: Agreeing on the family check-in changes
events.description: The team agreed to keep family names on screen and add one child at a time, while leaving payment as it is. Saved families, receipt editing, and a new dashboard are outside this change. Jordan can prepare it for the field check if the copy is final Monday. The staff note will stay a draft until it has been reviewed.

events.title: Making a Sunday coffee and walk plan
events.description: Maya, Alex, and I agreed to meet outside the café at 10:15 on Sunday, then walk along the river and back. I need to be home by 1 p.m. to call my parents. Maya asked me to bring the photo prints.

events.title: Offering to move the courtyard planters
events.description: Sarah asked for help with the large planters on Saturday. I can help at 1:30, before working on the shelf, and Matt will bring a hand truck. Sarah also offered some spare rosemary.

events.title: Planning the ending of the new song
events.description: Sam has booked the same room for tomorrow at 6:30 and shared the rough recording. We want to try stopping together after the last four bars. Alex will bring the guitar stand, and my bass cable is already packed.

events.title: Choosing the photo order before printing
events.description: The selection is down to 12 photos, from the bus window at the start to the empty basketball court at the end. Grace suggested swapping two street scenes, and Maya asked me to keep the blurry bakery window. I plan to print 10 rough copies during Friday’s lunch break.

events.title: Comparing the return flights for November
events.description: A Thursday arrival in Chicago looks best. Noah is free for dinner after 7, and Emma offered their couch before she and Ben drive to Madison around 4:30 Friday. I’m still choosing between two return flights; the cheaper one leaves too little time after the Sunday drive.

events.title: Reviewing the staff note with Luis and Marcus
events.description: We clarified that the family list is only for the current visit and clears after payment. Luis added that staff can check the names before charging. Marcus may use the two-child example after the field check, but the date in this draft isn’t a launch date.

events.title: Visiting Lakeside’s front desk
events.description: I watched a busy family check-in at Lakeside. After the visit, I focused on keeping family names visible during the current visit instead of adding a dashboard.

messages.content: Do you know yet if you can come for your dad's birthday? No pressure to fly in for one dinner.
I want to. I'm looking at the weekend of the 14th. Could stay with you if the spare room isn't full of tomato boxes.
Only one tomato box. I'll move it.
Can we keep Saturday pretty quiet? Dinner at home and maybe the lake if it's nice.
That is exactly what he wants. Emma said Friday after school is the earliest she can leave.
Okay. I'll work around that and send actual times once I've picked a flight.
Good. And tell me one thing you want to eat besides breakfast potatoes.
Mom says you're vetoing presents.
I'm not vetoing pie.
Very specific loophole. Apple?
Apple is good. Mostly I'd like to have everybody here for a meal.
Then no surprise restaurant reservation. We can cook and walk by the lake Saturday.
Perfect. There's a lamp in the garage we can take a look at if you get bored.
You really know how to sell a vacation.
I can get out of school around 4 on Friday. Ben can drive us up after that.
Would picking me up in Chicago make the drive annoying?
Depends where and when. Please don't book something that lands at 5:15 and assume we can be in Madison for dinner at 7.
Fair. I'll compare a Thursday arrival with flying straight to Madison. Budget is about $600 for travel.
Thursday would give you time to see Noah too. We need to be home Sunday by 7.
I'll leave Sunday lunch optional and build in the drive back. No packed itinerary.
For your dad's weekend: I can drive Friday and Sunday. Can you handle something easy for Friday dinner?
Yeah. Something Mom doesn't have to babysit while people arrive.
Chili? I can bring cornbread. Emma doesn't get an actual lunch break some Fridays, so let's not wait until nine.
Chili it is. I'll make it when I get to Madison, if Thursday works. Otherwise we can prep ahead.
Send me the grocery list when you've got one. No giant spreadsheet required.
You'll get a small list. I make no promises about whether it has headings.
Can we use tomorrow's review for drop-in passes? Lakeside's front desk is still writing sibling names on paper.
Yes. Priya saw the same thing Tuesday. Staff lose track of which child they're adding when they switch screens.
I don't think we need a family dashboard to solve that.
Agreed. I'll bring one option with a persistent family list and one with an add-another flow. Same scenario in both.
Good. We have thirty minutes, and Jordan needs a decision before Monday.
I'll lead with the choice and the reason. Screens after that.
The family list is straightforward. Letting people edit names inside the receipt is a different rabbit hole.
Let's keep editing in the form. Receipt can stay read-only.
Works for me. What happens if a parent adds three kids and backs up?
Keep all three names. Back should mean go back, not start over. I'll draw that state explicitly.
Thank you. That's the part I'd otherwise guess.
I'll post the two states before lunch. Feel free to call me if one doesn't make sense.
Pulled the notes from Lakeside. We watched seven family check-ins. In four, the receptionist wrote names on paper first.
Was that because of the screen or because the line was long?
Both. The screen only shows one child at a time, and they didn't want to ask the parent to repeat names.
Useful distinction. I'm going to keep the family names visible, but I won't claim it fixes the whole queue.
Exactly. Also, Kim at the desk asked us to stop calling it a household object.
Fair request. 'Family' on the screen, boring database names kept out of it.
Could you send me the plain-English version of the pass change? Three centers have asked.
It'll keep the family list on screen while staff add passes. Same payment step as now.
Does it save a family for next time? That's what the last caller thought.
No, just this visit. We should say that clearly in the note.

Helpful. Less elegant than our diagram, in a good way. One receptionist can talk to three people while finding a pen.
That's the job we're designing for. Show that messiness on Friday, not just the happy path.
Two options, same family checking in, and what happens when they back up.
Perfect. Don't spend Thursday night polishing the slide transitions.
I wasn't going to, but now you have successfully removed the temptation.

Maybe, but we haven't timed it. 'Keep a family's passes together' is something we can actually show.
Less punchy. More true. I can work with that.
Luis should read the draft first. People may think it saves the family for a future visit.
I'll put 'for this visit' in the first paragraph. Send me the final screen when Jordan has it.
Will do. We're aiming for next week's field check, not announcing a date yet.

Yes. 'Choose a pass for Jamie' tells staff what to fix. 'Missing selection' doesn't.
That's a better sentence. I'll change the other two errors while I'm here.
Great. Send the clickable version afterward; screenshots won't tell me where focus lands.
Tomorrow morning. I'm logging off for rehearsal soon.

The ones you've been 'almost done' with since August?

Happy to be ruthless. No laptop though.
Deal. Paper photos and coffee. Very advanced workflow.

Coffee with Maya first. Could do 10:30 if you don't mind me arriving fully caffeinated.
10:30 works. My friend Erin might come. Okay if I invite her?
Of course. Just tell her I am firmly in the climb-three-routes-and-chat camp.
That is also her camp.
Excellent. We have built a very achievable team.
I might put a shelf together this weekend. What time is least annoying downstairs?
Saturday afternoon is fine. Sunday I'm on an early shift, so quieter after eight would be lovely.
Saturday 2 to 4, then. It's freestanding, mostly the tiny wrench situation.
The tiny wrench is somehow the loudest tool.
I'll put a blanket under it. Also happy to move the courtyard planters first.
That would be great. They're heavy after the rain.
I'm in for October 17. Can do the bike table 10 to noon.
Amazing. Olivia has the back room until one. What do you need from us?
Two tables, a floor pump, and someone doing intake so I don't stop every five minutes.
I can handle intake for the first hour. Need to find someone for eleven.
Cap it at six bikes to start. Better to finish six than have twelve people annoyed.
Six slots. Walk-ins can still ask questions, but we won't promise a repair.
Back room is yours October 17, 10 to 1. A kids' class needs it at two, so please be packed by 1:30.
Thanks. We'll stop taking new items at noon and use the last half hour for cleanup.
Good. No extension cords across the main doorway this time.
We'll keep the electrical table along the back wall. I'll put it on the room sketch.
The center can cover $150. Anything beyond that needs to come from your group's budget.
Our total cap is $320. I'll send a simple supply list with who brings what.
Possibly in Chicago November 12, on the way to Dad's birthday. Dinner?
Yes, if by dinner you mean noodles and complaining about typography.
I was hoping we'd matured, but apparently not.
I can do Thursday after seven. Friday I'm helping my sister move.
Thursday sounds good. Don't block the whole night until I've actually booked.
Text me when it's real. I'll pick somewhere near the train so you don't spend the evening in a rideshare.
Book group next Thursday, 7 at the café. Bring one question, not a report.
You're taking away my ability to overprepare.
Yes. Last time you brought page flags in three colors.
This time my question is why nobody in this book ever just goes home.
Honestly, good question.
I'll finish the last forty pages on the bus. See you Thursday.
Wednesday: can we just work on the new song instead of playing the whole set?
Please. I still lose the count after the second chorus.
Let's loop that bit, then record one take. Room is booked 6:30 to 8:30.
I'll be there by 6:20. No work call this week.
Nice. I'll bring the little recorder.
And I'll bring the cable I forgot last time. Putting it in the bag now.
How many photos are in your twelve-photo zine now?
Twenty-six. In my defense, twelve is a difficult number.
It's actually one of the more straightforward numbers.
Maya helped me cut six. I think the bus-window shots belong together.
Then start there. Make a cheap print before you touch the color again.
Okay. Twelve images, folded paper, no new equipment. Hold me to it.
Happily. Mail me one when it's done.
Would a freestanding bookcase by the north wall be okay? About 5 feet tall, no drilling planned.
Yes. If the instructions call for anchors, send me a picture of the spot first. Old pipes are in part of that wall.
Got it. I'll choose something low enough to use safely without guessing about the wall.
Thanks. Also, I can look at the sticky window latch Friday around four.
I'll be home. It's still usable, just takes two hands.
I'll text before I come by.
Birthday weekend check: November 13 to 15. Ben and I drive up Friday after school.
The birthday person requests pie and no singing in a restaurant.
We can manage that.
I'm comparing flights. Saturday at home and a lake walk if the weather cooperates?
I'll bring a board game with rules shorter than the meal.
Sunday we'll need to leave by about 2 to be home in time.
Then lunch is optional, no cross-town detour. I'll put the actual arrival times in here once booked.
Sounds good. Really looking forward to it.
We have the back room October 17, 10 to 1. Chris can do six bike slots, with intake help.
I bring tools and a pump. Please don't put 'all repairs welcome' on the flyer.
I can do intake 11 to noon. Can we have a spot for people who just want advice?
Yes, small table by the windows. Main doorway has to stay clear.
Great. I'll do 10 to 11, Sarah does 11 to noon. New items stop at noon; cleanup starts at 12:30.
That's doable. I'd rather send someone home with an honest answer than rush a job.
Can the flyer say to bring the item, not just a photo of it? Last time was confusing.
Adding that, plus a line that a repair isn't guaranteed.
Review decision: keep the family list on screen; add one child at a time; payment stays as it is.
What are we deliberately leaving out?
Saved families for a later visit, receipt editing, and a new dashboard. This only helps today's check-in.
I can build that for the field check next Thursday if copy is final Monday.
I'll ask Lakeside for a quiet hour. We should test a family adding a child after backing up.
I'll read the staff note before it goes out. Please put 'for this visit' near the top.
Done. I'll send the note as a draft, not an announcement.
Good. I'll confirm the field visit with the center.
Weather looks decent Sunday morning. Coffee, then a short walk?
I'm up for it after ten. I can skip the gym one week.
Meet outside the café at 10:15? I need to be back by one to call my parents.
That gives us plenty of time. No destination?
Just along the river and back. I am resisting the urge to make a route.
Proud of you.
Bring the prints anyway. A bench can be a gallery.
Could either of you help move the big planters Saturday before it gets colder?
I can do 1:30, before the shelf project.
I'll bring a hand truck. Please don't try carrying the tall one down the steps.
Thank you. Also have spare rosemary if anyone wants some.
Yes please. My current plant collection is mostly empty pots.
Rosemary will improve the average.
Same room tomorrow, 6:30. I uploaded the rough recording.
The chorus is good. The ending sounds like three different exits.
Accurate. Can we try stopping together after the last four bars?
Yes. No dramatic fade-out, we are not that band.
I'll bring the guitar stand this time.
Bass cable is already packed. A historic first.
Here are the twelve. Bus window opens, empty basketball court closes.
That order makes sense. I'd swap the two middle street corners; the light moves more naturally.
Keep the blurry bakery window. It's the only one that feels warm.
I nearly cut that one. Okay, it stays.
Now print a rough copy. Screen decisions are done.
Friday lunch break. Ten cheap copies, then I can stop calling this a work in progress.
Thursday in Chicago seems best. Noah, dinner after seven still possible?
Yes. Pick a flight first and I'll keep dinner near wherever you're staying.
You can use our couch Thursday. Ben and I leave for Madison around 4:30 Friday.
That saves a hotel. I'll work from your kitchen Friday morning if that's okay.
Fine. The good chair is mine when I get home, though.
Understood. Still choosing between two return flights; one is cheaper but leaves too little time after the drive.
Draft is in the project. One correction: 'family list' isn't a saved profile. It clears after payment.
I added a sentence saying staff can check the names before charging. That's usually the question.

Noted. Draft stays a draft.

agentRooms.title: A week with room to breathe

messages.content: Work review Friday, rehearsal Wednesday, shelf Saturday. Why does that already feel like too much?
Because the preparation is floating around between the commitments. Give Thursday morning to the review, Friday lunch to the zine proof, and Saturday afternoon to the shelf. Leave tonight alone.
I still need to call Mom about November.
Sunday before one fits the walk you discussed with Maya and Alex. You already told them you need to be home. Put the call there instead of turning it into another evening task.
That feels better. Don't fill the empty bits.
Then the empty bits stay empty. The three preparation slots are enough for this week; the flight decision can wait until you have the two actual options.

agentRooms.title: A note for the front desk

messages.content: Make the staff note less like release notes.
Start with the situation: 'When a parent brings two children, add each pass while keeping both names in view.' Then explain that payment stays the same.
Could 'both' be confusing if there are three children?
Yes. 'Everyone's names' works better in the opening; keep two children just for the example. The note should also say the list is for this visit, not a saved family profile.
Keep it under a page.
It's now a short opening, one example, and the three questions Luis should check. No launch claim and no date that could be read as an announcement.
Olivia has $150 for supplies. Our whole cap is $320. How much are we actually asking our group to cover?
The planned supplies total $153, so the group covers $3 if those estimates hold. The $60 reserve is not planned spending. If you need all of it, the group's total contribution becomes $63.
So we shouldn't ask everybody for money as if we're spending $320.

Right. Say the current plan is $153 with a $60 reserve, funded first by the center's $150. Keep receipts and ask for any remaining shared cost after the event, using the arrangement the group agrees to.
Make the unspent bit obvious.
At the full $213 envelope, $107 of the cap is still unallocated. Having a cap does not make it a shopping target.
I feel guilty adding Chicago when the trip is supposed to be for Dad.
The Thursday stop can make the family part easier: it gives you a place to stay and the shared Friday ride. Dinner with Noah fits around that rather than taking time from Saturday.
Only if the flight isn't late.
Exactly. Keep dinner tentative until the flight is chosen. If you arrive late, skip dinner or make it brief; don't borrow time from the family day to rescue the extra plan.
And Sunday?
Protect the two o'clock departure from Madison. Compare return flights around that real constraint, not the other way around. I still need the actual options before recommending one.
Could I just squeeze the desk and shelf along the north wall?
The numbers say no: 42 plus 30 is 72 inches, and the available span is 58. You'd be fourteen inches short before leaving any clearance.
So adjacent wall first.
Yes. Measure width, depth, and the walking path. Then check the installation instructions. Freestanding in a listing doesn't automatically mean it is safe to skip an anchor the maker requires.
Matt wants a photo before anchors.
Take the photo after marking the proposed footprint with tape. That lets him see the exact wall area without you drilling anything.

agentRooms.title: What seven check-ins can tell us

messages.content: Four of seven families ended up on scrap paper. Can I put 57 percent on the slide?
The arithmetic is right, but the percentage would make seven observations look more representative than they are. Say four of the seven check-ins we watched, at one center.
What should the actual conclusion be?

Staff sometimes needed an outside place to keep names visible. The notes point to both the screen and a busy queue. A visible family list is worth trying; the notes do not prove it will remove the need for paper.
Then what do we watch next time?
Whether staff ask for names again, whether they reach for paper, and what happens when they go back to add another child. Keep the context beside each observation instead of making one big score.

agentRooms.title: Repair café: people, room, and money

messages.content: Check the plan together. I don't want to promise more than six bikes or accidentally spend the whole budget.
The schedule holds if new items stop at noon. Caspian covers intake 10–11 and Sarah 11–noon; Chris can work without restarting the conversation for every arrival.
Keep the questions table distinct from the repair queue and clear the doorway. Confirm the two tables with Olivia before drawing a final room plan.
Supplies are $153, with a $60 reserve. The $213 envelope leaves $107 unallocated. Tools come from volunteers, so no tool purchase belongs in this plan.
What would make us cut the number of slots?
If intake coverage falls through or Chris loses part of his two-hour window, reduce the offered slots before sharing the flyer. Don't keep six appointments by assuming he'll work faster.
I'll put those two checks above the volunteer list. The handoff document keeps the six-slot plan conditional on that coverage.
And the reserve stays separate from the shopping list.
I need one recommendation for Friday, and I don't want us to oversell the research.
Priya observed seven family check-ins and four uses of scrap paper. That supports examining visibility of names; it doesn't establish an average time saved.
Choose the persistent family list for the current visit. Leave saved families, receipt editing, and the dashboard out so Jordan can build the agreed change for the field check.
The decision line can be: 'Keep the family's names visible while staff add passes for this visit.' That's specific without a speed claim.
Put the back button in the review, not in a footnote.
It gets one of the two main walkthroughs: add a third child, then go back before payment. The existing names stay.
At the field visit, watch for repeated questions and separate paper notes. Treat those observations as the next input, not a victory already claimed.
Check the Chicago option together before I start treating it as a done deal.
It fits Thursday dinner with Noah and Friday's shared drive, but the return flight still has to allow for leaving Madison around two on Sunday.
The saved example numbers total $592, only $8 below the target after a $60 buffer. Replace them with actual quotes before deciding; a small fare change matters here.
Confirm the couch with both Emma and Ben, then send the family actual arrival times. Keep Saturday's lake walk weather-dependent and Sunday lunch optional.
So the next step is two real return options, not booking the outbound because it looks cheap.
Yes. Compare the whole trip around the shared drive. You don't yet have enough information to choose the early return.
Once the actual prices are in, we can say what changed and whether it still fits the $600 target.

# Family check-in: decision for Friday

**Choose the persistent family list for this visit.** Keep the existing payment step.

## Why this option

At Lakeside, four of seven observed family check-ins began with names written on paper. Priya’s notes connect this to a screen that shows one child at a time and staff wanting to avoid asking again. The design keeps the names visible; it does not yet prove that check-in is faster.

## What staff do

1. Add the first child and pass.
2. Keep that child in a visible family list while adding the next.
3. Check all names before payment.
4. If they go back, keep every entered name and selection.

## Thirty-minute review

- 0–5 minutes: replay the parent-with-two-children example.
- 5–10: choose the persistent list and state the limits.
- 10–20: inspect adding a third child and going back before payment.
- 20–25: review the name-specific error copy and keyboard order.
- 25–30: confirm owners: Caspian finishes copy, Jordan builds, Priya arranges the field visit, Luis checks the staff note.

## Out of scope

Saved families for future visits, editable receipts, and a new dashboard. The staff note must say **for this visit**.

## Next question

During the field visit, does the visible list reduce repeated questions or separate paper notes? Record what happens before making a speed claim.

artifacts.content:
# Dad’s birthday weekend · November 13–15

**Preferred outline: arrive in Chicago Thursday, share the drive Friday, keep Saturday for family.** Nothing is booked.

## Thursday, November 12

Arrive in Chicago early enough to get to Emma and Ben’s without rushing. Dinner with Noah after seven, near transit. Confirm dinner only after choosing the flight. Sleep on Emma and Ben’s couch.

## Friday

Work quietly from the kitchen in the morning. Pick up only the groceries that travel well. Leave for Madison around 4:30 after Emma gets home. Keep dinner easy; do not build an arrival promise around ideal traffic.

## Saturday: the birthday

Breakfast potatoes, time at home, and a lake walk if the weather is pleasant. Cook dinner together. Apple pie counts as the requested gift. No restaurant surprise and no singing requirement.

## Sunday

Breakfast together. Pack before noon. Lunch is optional, not another fixed event. Leave Madison around two so Emma and Ben can get home by evening. A return flight must leave enough margin after the drive; the early cheap option does not.

## Budget draft

| Item | Fictional estimate |
|---|---:|
| Round-trip flight through Chicago | $385 |
| Airport transit | $32 |
| Shared gas | $60 |
| Food allowance | $55 |
| Buffer | $60 |
| **Total** | **$592** |

The $600 target leaves only $8 outside the buffer. Check actual fares and schedules before deciding. Direct Madison routing totals $665 using the other sample quote.

## Still to decide

Choose the return flight after checking the Sunday drive. Then confirm Noah’s dinner and send the family the actual arrival times.

# A work corner that fits

**Keep the desk. Measure the adjacent wall before choosing a shelf.**

The north-wall span is 58 inches. The current desk is 42 inches wide; a 30-inch shelf next to it would need 72 inches. That arrangement does not fit.

## Before buying

- Measure the adjacent wall and walking clearance.
- Check shelf depth as well as width.
- Keep the window and radiator unobstructed.
- Read the manufacturer’s installation instructions. If anchors are required, ask Matt about the spot before drilling or deciding to omit them.
- Confirm transport; Caspian does not own a car.

## Budget

| Item | Fictional estimate |
|---|---:|
| Used low shelf | $65 |
| Task lamp | $35 |
| Cable clips | $12 |
| Transport reserve | $25 |
| **Planned total** | **$137** |
| **Remaining from $180** | **$43** |

## Saturday

1:30: help move the courtyard planters with Sarah and Matt.

2–4: assemble on a blanket, check the feet and stability, and clear the packaging.

Afterward: sit at the desk with the lamp on before deciding whether anything else is needed. Leave the $43 unspent until the basic arrangement feels right.

No purchase or wall modification has been authorized by this plan.

For Luis to review before sharing. No release date has been announced.

In the version we’ll try at the next field visit, you can keep a family’s names on screen while adding passes **for this visit**. It does not save a family profile for next time.

For example, add Jamie’s pass, then add Casey’s. Both names stay in the list so you can check them before taking payment. If you go back to change a pass, the names you already entered stay there.

The payment step works as it does today. If a pass is missing, the message names the person who needs one, such as “Choose a pass for Jamie.”

Questions to check at the field visit:

- Can staff tell which person they are adding a pass for?
- Is it clear that the list applies only to this visit?
- Does going back behave as they expect?

Luis reviews the wording first. Marcus may use the example after the field check; this draft is not an announcement.

# Twelve photos, finished

**A few walks, a few bus rides, and the things I almost passed.**

Portland · August–September 2026

## Sequence already decided

Open with the bus window. Keep the blurry bakery window. Swap the two middle street corners as Grace suggested. Close with the empty basketball court. Keep the total at twelve.

## Friday lunch break

1. Export the agreed sequence. Do not restart the color edit.
2. Print one inexpensive proof.
3. Fold it and check page order, margins, and whether anything important falls into the fold.
4. Fix only a visible printing problem.
5. Print ten copies. Write the month and year inside the back cover.

## Where the copies go

One for Grace, one for Maya, one to keep. Leave the other seven unassigned rather than inventing a distribution project.

## Done means

A folded copy can be held and read. A new camera, a website, and a longer introduction are not needed. Mailing Grace’s copy comes after printing; no mailing has happened yet.
